The requested wording changes concern the landing-page hero and prize section, not the FAQ content.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
hmmmmm, I actually prefer the way you had it before.
The top of the landing page looks a bit messy now with the huge writing and large photo overlapping the 'view dashboard' button.

I liked the 'Project Rebuild' you had at the top before with the subtitles, and the whole layout, etc.

I wanted to change some of the wording (but you don't have to go character for character either, if it looks or feels messy or too repetitive or salesy), and I wanted to add bolding for emphasis to selling points, like '$500 random giveaway every 100 sales' or '$5 unlimited, instant commission' instead of having those selling points in brackets.

And I wanted to have the ebook cover on the landing page somewhere... it can be any size, whatever fits the aesthetics.

And it looks like the cover picture i sent you still needs to be cropped slightly.. can you do that or you want me to?

need to change 'win $500 every 100 sales!' to '$500 giveaway every 100 sales'.
and can drop 'constant little cracks at $500' and just leave it at '1 affiliate selected from each 100 sales block. More referrals = more chances to win!'
can also drop 'ongoing roulette spin:'

(my toddlers are driving me crazy right now, but ill be back in a little bit)

value_updates.placement: any aesthetically suitable location on the landing page
value_updates.cover_image_cropping: Crop the supplied cover image slightly.

decisions.reason: The source changes marketing wording and emphasis but does not alter the existing $5 commission or one-ticket-per-successful-referral mechanics.
The source does not change how commissions or prize tickets are represented in the dashboard.
The phrase about more referrals producing more chances restates the existing weighting rule and does not change ticket counters, eligibility windows, or post-draw handling.
Removing Chainlink terminology from a landing-page sentence does not cancel or modify the underlying on-chain Chainlink VRF winner-selection requirement.
The source discusses coded-referral marketing copy and does not address reward routing when no referral code is supplied.
The source changes prize-section wording but does not alter automatic payout, winner announcements, or notification channels.
The landing-page copy revision does not change the $15 mint revenue split or active prize-pool allocation.
The replacement wording restates the existing one-$500-winner-per-100-sales mechanism without changing winner count, prize amount, trigger, or eligible population.
